summary.text: Gabe Amo is the Democratic incumbent for Rhode Island's 1st District, first elected in a November 2023 special election. A Pawtucket native, he worked in the Obama White House, for Governor Gina Raimondo, on Joe Biden's 2020 campaign, and in the Biden White House before running for Congress. His official site lists retirement security, gun violence, climate resilience, reproductive freedom and protecting democracy among his priorities.

paragraphs.text: Born in 1987 and a native of Pawtucket, Rhode Island, according to Ballotpedia and his official biography; he is the son of a mother from Liberia and a father from Ghana.

Graduated from Moses Brown School in Providence and earned a B.A. in political science from Wheaton College in Norton, Massachusetts, where, per his official biography, he graduated summa cum laude and Phi Beta Kappa, was student government president, and was named a Truman Scholar.
After college, received a Marshall Scholarship to study at the University of Oxford, according to his official biography.
Earlier in his career, served in the Office of Public Engagement and Intergovernmental Affairs for President Barack Obama as a liaison to governors and state government officials.

Worked as director of public engagement and community affairs for then-Rhode Island Governor Gina Raimondo, serving as her principal advisor to the state's cities and towns, business, labor, advocacy, and faith communities.
Worked as a states-strategy and program advisor on Joe Biden's 2020 presidential campaign.

Served as special assistant to the President and deputy director of the White House Office of Intergovernmental Affairs under President Biden, as principal liaison to mayors and local elected officials.
Won the November 7, 2023 special general election for the seat vacated by David Cicilline, defeating Republican Gerry Leonard, and was re-elected in November 2024 over Republican Allen Waters.
Serves on the House Foreign Affairs Committee (as vice ranking member), the Science, Space, and Technology Committee (as ranking member of its Environment Subcommittee), and the Budget Committee.
